 Here's What You'll Pay for iPhone Duo Repairs Without AppleCare+ (Spoiler: It's a Lot)
 Clumsy? Good luck.
 By
 Devesh Beri
 October 22, 2026
 Share on Facebook (opens in a new window) 
 Share on X (opens in a new window) 
 Share on Reddit (opens in a new window) 
 Share on Hacker News (opens in a new window) 
 Share on Flipboard (opens in a new window) 
 Credit: Apple 
 US-based iPhone Duo owners who skip AppleCare+ could face repair charges ranging from $49 for minor damage to $1,499 for more severe workups. Without the extended warranty and accidental damage coverage, Apple's highest repair estimate is roughly 75% of the phone's $1,999 starting price. 
 According to updated Apple support documentation, repairing the iPhone Duo's inner display costs $999 without AppleCare+ and $99 with it, making it the most expensive individual component repair on the list. Thankfully, replacing only the nano-texture cover layer on the inner screen costs just $49 ($19 with AppleCare+). This is how you "reset" the foldable's inner crease .
 Outer display repairs are $379 (versus $29), and back-glass repairs are $199 (also versus $29). Damage affecting both the outer display and back glass carries a combined $509 estimate, but would cost less than $60 with AppleCare+ coverage.
 iPhone users can replace their phone's battery if its health meter sits under 80%. Without the extended warranty, the iPhone Duo's battery costs $229 to replace, but AppleCare+ subscribers get it free. 
 Does this make purchasing AppleCare+ an easy decision? Not really. In the US, AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss costs $19.99 monthly or $199.99 annually. If you like to make your phone last rather than buy the latest model every year, you could spend hundreds of dollars on AppleCare+ coverage over the device's life. That said, one annual payment plus a $99 inner display replacement would "only" total $298.99 before taxes—significantly less than $999 for the same repair. If you're clumsy, maybe purchasing additional coverage is the right move for you.
